test_title: SSC GD Constable (2022) Official Paper (Held On : 10 Jan 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My aunt Geeta, / is knowing / my friend Rudransh / very well.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **segment** that contains a grammatical **error** is **"is knowing".**
 
• In English, the verb **"know"** is a stative verb, not an action verb, meaning it describes a state or condition, not an action that is happening.
 
• Therefore, it's not typically used in the continuous tense. The** correct form **should be **"knows".**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** would be: *"My aunt Geeta knows my friend Rudransh very well."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's a brief explanation of the other options:
 
 
• **"Very well" **- This is an adverb phrase used to describe the extent of the verb. In this case, it's used to indicate the depth of knowledge or familiarity. There's no error here.
 
• **"My aunt Geeta" -** This is a proper noun phrase serving as the subject of the sentence. There's no error in this segment.
 
• **"My friend Rudransh" **- This is a noun phrase serving as the object of the sentence. Again, there's no error in this segment.
